business_scope.primary_industry_name: Competitive Gaming Matchmaking and Tournament Systems

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-Argentina BIT (1990), Spain-Brazil BIT (1994), Spain-Chile BIT (1991), Spain-Mexico BIT (1997), Spain-Peru BIT (1994), and multiple DTAs with EU member states and Latin American jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Ley 7/2021, de 5 de noviembre, de medidas urgentes para la adaptación normativa en materia de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y la financiación del terrorismo

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Equivalent from Foreign Jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) using Spanish Guardia Civil lists, Europol, OFAC SDN List, UN Sanctions List, and Spanish AML/CFT database; full KYC for UBOs including source of wealth

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) through the Sede Electrónica del Registro Mercantil
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Spanish; foreign words permitted but must be adapted to Spanish orthography; no foreign characters outside Latin alphabet
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms implying public or official status such as 'Banco', 'Caja de Ahorros', 'Ayuntamiento', 'Gobierno'; vulgar or obscene language; names that could mislead the public regarding the company's nature or activities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the Ministry of Justice within 1 month from notification of the rejection

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible; a virtual office must provide a physical address in Spain for service of process and may be used for registered office of SL
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for pre-incorporation phase; post-incorporation unannounced inspections by tax authorities or commercial registry are possible but infrequent for standard SL entities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal and Notarial Fees for SL Formation

Annual subscription fee for compliant registered office

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation and Certification of Foreign Documents

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Articles 1, 2, 20-23, 58, 62, 66, 175-178, 209-216 and 231); supplemented by Ley 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre, de apoyo a los emprendedores (electronic incorporation via CIRCE and optional Formación Sucesiva SL with EUR 1 capital).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office province; the deed is executed by a Notario and filed electronically via CIRCE / Ventanilla Única Empresarial.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) with adopted estatutos sociales, submitted for mandatory inscription in the Registro Mercantil.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SL minimum share capital is EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash before deed execution, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) issued by a Spanish credit institution and annexed to the public deed; the funds remain blocked until registration. Alternative regime: Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva under Ley 14/2013 with EUR 1 capital but subject to dividend restrictions, minimum legal reserve obligations, and dissolution triggers; standard ES_SL template applies EUR 3,000 paid-up capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST: The incorporation deed and articles of association having been executed and approved, all capital subscriptions of EUR 3,000, fully paid in, are ratified; the administrator is directed to complete Commercial Registry registration and convert the provisional tax code. SECOND: The registered office is fixed at Calle Gran Vía 42, Planta 3, 28013 Madrid, Spain, within the Madrid commercial registry district; management may relocate offices within the same province without an extraordinary resolution. THIRD: [Full Name] is appointed Sole Administrator with full powers to open and operate bank accounts, appoint agents, sign membership and payment-rail agreements, and procure the esports, data-protection and municipal licenses for the business. FOURTH: All governmental filings incidental to incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) via CIRCE / Ventanilla Única Empresarial online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name-application request to the RMC certifying that the proposed denomination is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing corporate name. Provide at least three alternative names in priority order. The certificate is normally issued electronically within one to two working days and remains valid for a limited period for deed execution.
required_dossiers: Online name application form (modelo de certificación de denominación social)
List of proposed corporate names in priority order
Passport or national identity card of each founder
Proof of reserved name payment (RMC fee)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RMC objects on grounds of similarity or identity, resubmit within the validity window using the next alternative name; if the certificate expires, request a fresh reservation from the RMC before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital subscription and blocked bank deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (entidad de crédito) authorized by the Banco de España, e.g., Santander, CaixaBank, or Ibercaja
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate account (cuenta de constitución) in the names of the founders, deposit the full minimum capital of EUR 3,000 in cash, and obtain a bank certificate of deposit and block (certificado de desembolso) for annexation to the Notary deed. The certificate must identify the depositors, the account number, and the blocked amount.
required_dossiers: RMC name reservation certificate
Passports / nationality IDs of all subscribing founders
Draft deed or articles of association (estatutos) reflecting share distribution
Bank KYC forms, source-of-funds declaration, and tax residence declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional anti-money-laundering documentation, provide apostilled identity evidence, source-of-funds statements, and a professional reference; alternatively, use a notary-managed capital escrow arrangement to satisfy the statutory payment-in requirement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the public incorporation deed before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario (Notary Public) of the province where the registered office will be located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend the notarial appointment personally or by duly authorized attorney-in-fact, review and sign the Escritura de Constitución, approve the estatutos sociales (governing structure, share transfers, board powers), and include the capital deposit certificate and administrators' acceptances. The notary will issue the primera copia and submit the deed electronically to the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: RMC name reservation certificate (original)
Bank certificate of paid-up and blocked capital
Certified Spanish identification of each founding member and appointed administrator
Established articles of association signed by all founders
Consent letters of the appointed Sole Administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies statutory defects or omissions, the founders execute a correcting instrument (escritura de subsanación) before the same notary; if a founder is unavailable, proceed through a documentary power of attorney executed under Spanish law and notarized abroad with apostille.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), local tax office or online with X.509 certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the month following execution of the deed, file form 036 (Censo de Obligados Tributarios) attaching a simple copy of the deed and the administrator's identification, requesting the provisional NIF (starting with letter N). The provisional NIF is mandatory before Commercial Registry inscription and is subsequently converted to the definitive NIF after registration.
required_dossiers: Form 036 duly signed by the administrator
Simple copy (copia simple) of the notarial incorporation deed
Details of the registered office and planned activity (ISIC 5820 / CNAE 5820 software publishing)
Identity document of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT requests corrections or supplementary documentation, respond within the granted term by submitting a certified simple copy of the deed and a signed authorization; if the request is time-barred, file a rectification form and request reactivation of the census entry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry registration and legal personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of Madrid (registered office province)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified first copy of the deed (primera copia) with the Registro Mercantil Provincial through the notary's electronic channel. The registrar will review the deed and statutes for legality (calificación registral) and, upon approval, inscribe the company in the commercial registry; registration vests the SL with full legal personality. After inscription, verify the definitive NIF and notify the bank to release the blocked capital.
required_dossiers: First copy (primera copia) of the notarial deed
RMC name reservation certificate (annexed to deed)
Proof of provisional NIF application submitted to AEAT
AEAT census form 036 acknowledgment
Bank certificate of deposit and block
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a nota de defectos, correct the deficiencies by supplementary notarial instrument or administrative documentation within the statutory cure period; if registration is refused, appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública or file new documentation, as applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration opening, corporate governance books, and optional activity licenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT (definitive NIF), Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (if hiring), and Ayuntamiento de Madrid / Ventanilla Única Empresarial (only if a physical office or esports venue is opened)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the definitive NIF (form 036 update), adopt the mandatory corporate books (libro registro de socios, book of minutes, register of contracts with the sole administrator), register as employer if personnel will be hired, open the definitive operating bank account, and, if physical premises are leased, submit a declaración responsable or solicitud de licencia de apertura together with the fire-safety certificate. For the pure digital esports platform, no industrial operating license is mandated.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Commercial Registry inscription (certificación literal)
Definitive NIF document issued by AEAT
Copy of the estatutos and incorporating deed for corporate books
Social security employer registration form TA.6 if employees are recruited
Municipal activity declaration (declaración responsable) and fire-safety documentation if a physical office or event venue is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality queries the activity declaration, supplement the technical dossier (layout plan, occupancy certificate, fire-safety compliance) or convert to a full licencia de apertura procedure; if AEAT delays the definitive NIF, submit the registration certificate and request urgent processing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial manufacturing, warehouse, or physical production installation. If a physical office, esports venue, or public-event facility is opened: Ayuntamiento de Madrid — Área de Gobierno de Obras y Equipamientos / Oficina de Licencias through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial, with regional oversight by the Consejería de Economía, Hacienda y Empleo de la Comunidad de Madrid for public esports events.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No mandatory operating permit for the pure digital esports matchmaking and tournament platform (ISIC 5820 / CNAE 5820). For any leased premises or intermittent tournament venue, the applicable authorization is the municipal Licencia de Apertura or, for lower-impact premises, the Declaración Responsable de Actividad; public esports tournaments with spectators require the Licencia de Espectáculos Públicos y Actividades Recreativas of the Autonomous Community of Madrid.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD); regional counterpart: Consejería de Medio Ambiente, Agricultura e Interior de la Comunidad de Madrid
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no environmental impact assessment required. The esports community platform is a digital service with no industrial installation, no substantial land use, and negligible direct emission footprint; only ordinary tertiary-sector office activity is contemplated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous-waste discharge in the platform's own operations. If an office is leased, comply with Ley 7/2022 de residuos y suelos contaminados (transposing EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC) for separated urban waste streams, and with municipal waste collection ordinances; electrical and electronic equipment must be handled through authorized WEEE channels.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defense structural or industrial load permits apply to the platform activity, which is hosted on cloud infrastructure. For any leased office or esports venue, obtain: (1) fire-safety compliance certificate under CTE DB-SI and periodic inspections per RIPCI; (2) occupancy-load clearance for public tournament areas; and (3) a workplace risk assessment and prevention plan under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including ergonomic workstation evaluations, first-aid provisions, and appointment of a prevention officer where employee thresholds are met.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es (Sede Electrónica).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada): (1) obtain negative name certificate from Registro Mercantil Central; (2) execute public deed before a notary; (3) file Model 036 with AEAT to request the provisional NIF (format B-XXXXXXXX); (4) register the company in the Registro Mercantil within the legal term; (5) obtain the definitive NIF and the statistical card (tarjeta estadística). Foreign enterprises without a permanent establishment but with taxable supplies in Spain must obtain an NIF for non-residents by filing Model 036 through a tax representative, attaching apostilled constitutional documents and a certificate of residence of the foreign entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the SL is a fully tax-transparent entity; resident SLs are subject to Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at the 25% headline rate (23%/21% reduced SME rate for tax periods 2023-2024/2025+ where net turnover < €1M; 15% reduced rate for newly created entities in year 1-2 if the activity is not subject to an undistributed profits reserve limitation). Non-resident shareholders are subject to non-resident income tax (IRNR) on distributions and capital gains; Spain applies the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive 0% withholding rate for qualifying corporate shareholders. Territorial scope: worldwide taxation for resident companies, with foreign tax credit; the SL can opt for tax consolidation under Article 64 LIS once the 70%/75% group participation test is met.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain operates no US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is fixed by the corporate form (LIS Article 8). Available elections include: (i) tax consolidation group regrouping (Art. 64-67 LIS) upon prior communication to AEAT; (ii) application of the special VAT simplified scheme (Model 037) and agriculture/forestry/livestock scheme where turnover ceilings are met; (iii) the Union One-Stop Shop (OSS) non-Union OSS and Import OSS schemes for distance sales and B2C digital services; (iv) accelerated R&D&I tax credits (Art. 35 LIS); (v) the Patent Box regime (Art. 23 LIS) for qualifying IP; (vi) Spanish non-resident tax registration designations (PE vs. isolated operation vs. Art. 12.5 IRNR seizure election); and (vii) reversal of the burden of the anti-hybrid rules of Art. 15.f) and 62 LIS under ATAD transposition (Law 22/2021), requiring taxpayers to pre-emptively disclose hybrid mismatch outcomes in Model 023 (cross-border arrangements, DAC6) where materialized.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), harmonized in Spain by Ley 37/1992 (LIVA) and RD 1624/1992; territorial regime supplemented by Basque Country and Navarra foráis (own VAT administrations: Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa, Araba and Hacienda Tributaria de Navarra).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de-minimis exemption threshold: any taxable person habitually carrying out taxable economic activities in Spanish territory must apply for a VAT number (NIF-IVA, followed by the ES prefix for intra-EU) before starting the activity via Model 036/037. For the optional simplified scheme (régimen simplificado) eligibility, prior-year net turnover must not exceed €250,000 for goods resale or €125,000 for services; for distance sales into Spain, the intra-EU distance-selling threshold is €10,000 (unionwide OSS option).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time/incremental fiscal clearance is implemented through two systems: (i) SII — Suministro Inmediato de Información (RD 596/2016; effective since 2017): obliged businesses (>€6M turnover, VAT groups, foreign registration category 151, etc.) must upload invoice records to AEAT within 4 calendar days (8 days for certain records and amendments) in XML schema 3.1; (ii) Verifactu (RD 1007/2023, mandatory for all billing software at issuer level from April 2025 and compulsory as business accounting support from April 2026): requires software suppliers to obtain a verifiable declaration of conformity, QR codes and digital traceability for each invoice. Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) mandates B2B e-invoicing exchange on a state digital invoice platform (solution available as of 2024; mandatory within one/two-year deadline by company size depending on regulation date). Non-compliance carries the penalties of Ley 58/2003 (LGT) and specific SII-formalities penalties up to €10,000 per omission.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods to non-EU destinations are exempt with credit (0% VAT) under Art. 21.1 LIVA, provided the goods leave the EU customs territory; the export must be evidenced and the dispatch must occur within 90 days of the invoiced supply (Art. 22 LIVA; extension permitted by customs). Digital and esports platform services: B2B cross-border supplies to non-EU or EU customers follow the B2B place-of-supply rule (customer establishment), so Spanish VAT is not levied/reverse-charged; for B2C remote digital services to final consumers in other Member States, the Union OSS regime allows the platform to self-assess the destination-country VAT (Spanish standard rate 21%), while supplies to non-EU consumers fall outside Spanish VAT entirely; the sale of physical merchandising exported from Spain to non-EU customers qualifies for the Art. 21 export exemption. The exporter must have obtained the customs export declaration (DUA/EX) and dispose of the goods at the time of departure.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD — Documento Único Administrativo) XOR ECS electronic export summary declaration
Proof of exit: customs stamp, Sortie Certificate, or in-house computer check (E-portal) under Art. 795 of EU Reg. 2015/2447
Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill or equivalent transport title that unequivocally evidences the non-EU destination
Commercial invoice and proforma export contract
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT credit advice showing collection of the foreign-exchange proceeds
Banking settlement and repatriation statements (Model 036/declaración informativa de operaciones con el exterior) for exchange-control evidence
Internal movement records (ALLE-DOT) if the dispatch is made from bonded warehouses

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain); foreign exchange administration is jointly executed with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOMEX) under the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise (Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa) for investment declarations and balance-of-payments statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible; Spain maintains no exchange controls. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are liberalized under EU Treaty provisions (TFEU Articles 63-66) and Spanish Law 19/2003 on capital movements. Profit remittance by an SL is unrestricted subject only to corporate tax compliance, certification of non-domiciled payment flows, and standard AML documentation; no prior administrative authorization is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Spain. Exporters and providers of digital services may freely retain foreign currency proceeds in resident or non-resident bank accounts, with no timeline or repatriation deadline, though receipts must be booked for balance-of-payments reporting when they affect Spain's international investment position.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-High for EU/EEA-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) passporting into Spain under PSD2 and the EBA passport regime (e.g., N26, Qonto, Berkay); these can provide SEPA and SWIFT rails with fully compliant Spanish IBANs. Offshore non-EU EMIs and unlicensed neobanks are Low viability and effectively barred from offering payment accounts to an ES_SL without a Spanish or EEA license due to Banco de España registration requirements and AML Law 10/2010 restrictions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted for resident directors using video identification and electronic signature, but major Spanish banks typically require at least one managing director with an NIE to appear physically or via notarized power of attorney for non-resident UBOs and when opening escrow-bound accounts. A Spanish fiscal representative is mandatory for onboarding where the majority of UBOs are non-EU residents, and enhanced due diligence interviews are conducted in-practice for all non-resident ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO structure where esports tournament prize flows involve global players or aggregator payment wallets without clear identification of final beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified UBO registry extract (Registro de Titularidades Reales), notarized organizational chart, passport copies of all natural-person UBOs, corporate register certificate (Certificación del Registro Mercantil), and a written description of the tournament prize pool custody and disbursement flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk source-of-funds concentration from crypto-currency prize payouts or gambling-adjacent jurisdictions flagged by bank sanctions screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent audit of platform wallet balances, transactional ledger history tracing inbound funds to identifiable commercial counterparties, player-payout policy governing taxes and chargebacks, exchange/wallet provider license evidence, and confirmation that the platform does not involve regulated gambling services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border revenue concentration from Latin American markets triggering enhanced transfer and corresponder-bank scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial agreements with LatAm distribution partners, transfer pricing documentation (Form 232 and Chapter VI OECD TP report if applicable), customer and counterparty KYC files, bank statements of related collection entities, and a treasury management policy demonstrating upstream tax withholdings and intercompany loan/fee governance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity or shareholder loan injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank) to the ES_SL's euro-denominated operational account quoting purpose code 1010-capital subscription (or 1120-loans) under the Bank of Spain Balance of Payments classification; the foreign investment must be reported post-investment through DGCOMEX Form D-1A if the non-resident investor holds at least 10% or the transaction exceeds EUR 3,000,000, with the SL's NIE tax ID and registered address validated before credit confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: International disbursements use SWIFT MT103 for direct correspondent-bank payments to non-EU suppliers and SEPA CT (ISO 20022 pain.001) for EU/EEA counterparts; for high-value esports tournament licensing or strategic acquisitions, irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit and standby credits are issued through Santander/CaixaBank trade desks, while LatAm collections may be consolidated via treasury pooling and cleared through SWIFT or local clearing systems (e.g., SPEI in Mexico) with NDF coverage.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/LatAm currency forwards (deliverable) with authorized Spanish credit entities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid currencies such as ARS, COP, and VES where physical settlement is prohibited
Cross-currency swaps (EUR vs USD/GBP) for hedging long-term intercompany loan or tournament guarantee exposures
Vanilla FX options (EUR calls/puts) for asymmetric mitigation on tournament prize pools and licensing milestone receipts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts deposit (Cuentas Anuales) comprising Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Statement of Changes in Equity, Notes, and Management Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Mercantile Registry of the registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' ordinary general meeting must approve the accounts within six months of the fiscal year end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); deposit with the Registry within one month of approval, thus no later than 31 July for calendar-year filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalty from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 under Royal Decree 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital) if the deposit is not made within the legal period; closure of the company's open registry sheet after six months of non-deposit; inability to obtain a certificate of good standing and limitation on inscribing corporate acts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year; for a 31 December year-end, by 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge (recargo de extemporaneidad) of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% depending on the delay, plus late-payment interest (currently 3.75%); fixed penalties ranging from EUR 200 to EUR 20,000 for non-presentation or inaccurate filings; administrative enforcement by AEAT including embargo of assets

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit where at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: total assets above EUR 2,846,000; net annual revenue above EUR 5,699,000; average workforce above 50 employees. Audit is also required for companies belonging to a consolidation group or carrying out regulated activities under specific statutes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad, PGC) in accordance with the Código de Comercio and the Spanish Companies Act; consolidated accounts of groups using EU-adopted IFRS; all accounts presented in euros with notes and prior-year comparatives.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO declaration is required in Spain. The Sociedad de Limitada must maintain a permanent internal register of ultimate beneficial owners (Libro de Titulares Reales) and file any transfer of shares or change of control with the Registro Mercantil within 30 days. The annual accounts must reflect relevant UBO-related disclosures and director shareholding details.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Libro de Titulares Reales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,800 per annum for registered office services and professional corporate secretarial agent in Madrid or Barcelona
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 9,000 per annum for a small or mid-size Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate for newly created SLs on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base (20% on the excess) for the first two tax periods with positive taxable income (Art. 29.1 LIS 27/2014); capitalization reserve reducing taxable base by 10% of the increase in net equity, capped at 10% of pre-reserve taxable base (Art. 25 LIS); levelling reserve for small entities of 10% (Art. 105 LIS); R&D tax credit of 25% (42% on incremental spend) and technology innovation credit of 12% (Art. 33 LIS); patent box nexus-based relief (Art. 23 LIS); 30% video game production tax credit applicable to qualifying esports software and platform development costs (Art. 36 ter LIS).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Modelo 200) - Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades); filed exclusively via the AEAT electronic headquarters (Sede Electronica de la Agencia Estatal de Administracion Tributaria) using an electronic certificate, DNIE or Cl@ve PIN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six months after the tax year-end. For a calendar-year SL, filing must be completed by 25 July of the following year. A different fiscal year may be adopted only if expressly provided in the bylaws; the deadline then runs from that fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF - Spanish tax identification number of the legal entity (format A/B/C/J followed by eight digits, with control letter).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident entity acting through a Spanish permanent establishment must use the PE's own NIF; a foreign parent NIF is not accepted. A non-resident without a PE is outside Form 200 and files Form 210 instead.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period start and end dates; the return must cover the exact fiscal year adopted by the SL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must adopt the same fiscal year as its foreign head office where the head office's accounting period is used for Spanish bookkeeping; otherwise calendar-year convention applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result before tax (resultado contable) per Spanish GAAP financial statements; the mandatory starting point of the tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs compute the accounting result from their separately kept Spanish books using the same allocation rules as the head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate permanent adjustments to the accounting result (correcciones al resultado contable): non-deductible expenses, non-taxable income, depreciation timing differences and transfer pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs add back head-office general expenses allocated to Spain only where supported by documentation and economically justified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before offset of prior-year negative taxable bases and before capitalization and levelling reserve reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs must offset losses previously recognised by the same Spanish PE; losses of the foreign head office are not included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capitalization reserve reduction under Art. 25 LIS, limited to the smaller of 10% of the increase in net equity and 10% of the taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reserve is likewise available to a PE only if the foreign entity records the equivalent reserve in its head-office accounts and meets the equity maintenance test.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year negative taxable bases (compensacion de bases imponibles negativas), mandatorily declared in the order of generation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs may only offset negative bases previously computed in the same Spanish PE; losses are not transferable from the head office or other group entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable base (base imponible) after offset and reserve reductions; the amount to which the corporate tax rate is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs apply the same rates; the PE's taxable base must reflect only Spanish-sourced activity and assets under Art. 22 RDL 5/2004.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable statutory rate: 25% general; 15% for new entities on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable base and 20% on the excess; special rates for certain entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs of foreign entities use the general 25% rate; the reduced new-entity rate is not available to a PE of an existing foreign company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability (cuota integra): taxable base at the applicable rate before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs compute the same amount and then claim treaty benefits, where applicable, through the corresponding box instead of withholding relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax deductions and credits: double taxation relief, R&D and innovation credits, video game production credit, patent box, and reinvestment relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs claim credits strictly proportional to Spanish-sourced income and may not claim credits that are restricted to resident entities unless a DTA provides otherwise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax liability (cuota liquida): gross liability reduced by deductions but before withholding credits and instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must reconcile the result with its foreign head-office computation where the DTA uses the credit method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings made on the entity's income, quarterly instalment payments (Form 202), and payments on account already made during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs include Spanish withholdings suffered on interest, dividends and royalties sourced in Spain; foreign tax credits are not entered here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Differential result (cuota diferencial): the final amount payable to the AEAT or refundable to the taxpayer.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made in euros from a Spanish bank account; refunds are remitted to the PE's Spanish account or to the foreign head office upon request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Voluntary late filing without prior AEAT notice triggers a progressive surcharge under Art. 27 LGT of 5% of tax due within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months and 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest. Compulsory late filing after AEAT notice attracts fixed penalties under Art. 198 LGT of EUR 150 to EUR 1,500, or, if collection is affected, 2% of the relevant tax amount. Substantial underdeclaration is penalised at 50% to 150% of the evaded tax under Art. 191 LGT. Loss of Form 200 filing rights may invalidate loss offsets and tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 202 (Modelo 202) - Quarterly Corporate Income Tax Instalment Payment (Pago Fraccionado); and Form 222 (Modelo 222) for entities that are members of a tax consolidation group; both filed via the AEAT Sede Electronica.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by the 20th day of April, October and December respectively for the 3-month, 6-month and 9-month periods ending on 31 March, 30 September and 30 November; for a calendar-year taxpayer the instalment calendar is 20 April, 20 October and 20 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF of the entity making the instalment payment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE uses its Spanish PE NIF; instalments are computed only on the PE's Spanish results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax period of the current return and the month covered by the instalment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE follows the same tax period as the head office where possible; otherwise calendar-year intervals apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculation base under the method elected in Art. 40.3 LIS: either the final corporate tax liability (cuota integra) of the preceding tax period, or the accounting profit accrued from the first day of the tax period to the day immediately preceding the instalment deadline.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs use the PE-specific preceding-year liability or the PE's own accrued accounting profit; the method must be consistent for all instalments of the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Percentage applied to the base: 20% when using the prior-year cuota integra method; 17% of the year-to-date accounting profit for entities with annual turnover below EUR 10 million; 0% for newly created entities during the first two tax periods.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PEs are generally excluded from the 0% option and apply the standard 17% or 20% percentages.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount to pay to the AEAT, net of withholdings and of instalments already paid earlier in the same year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made by SEPA direct debit or electronic transfer; underpayment generates late-payment interest from the original instalment due date.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted instalments accrue late-payment interest and are offset by the AEAT against the final annual assessment. The progressive surcharge and penalties of Art. 27 and Art. 198 LGT apply as for the annual return; deliberate understatement attracts the 50% to 150% penalty of Art. 191 LGT on the underpaid instalment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% statutory withholding on dividends, profit distributions and participation in profits paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident shareholder without a Spanish permanent establishment (Art. 25.1 of RDL 5/2004, Non-Resident Income Tax Law). The 19% rate also applies where the distribution is made through an intermediary account holder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA (Spain has over 100 treaties) the non-resident shareholder must: (1) obtain an officially certified Certificate of Fiscal Residence (TRC) from its jurisdiction of residence covering the calendar year of the distribution; (2) deliver the TRC to the Spanish paying SL before the dividend payment date, together with proof of beneficial ownership and, where the reduced treaty rate depends on holding, evidence of the minimum shareholding (commonly 10% or 25%) and the minimum holding period (commonly 1 year or 2 years) under the relevant treaty; (3) the Spanish payer may then reduce the withholding at source to the treaty rate (typically 5% or 10%); the supporting documents must be retained in the SL's file and reported through the annual Form 296 information return; (4) if the full 19% was withheld, the non-resident recovers the excess by filing Form 210 (Non-Resident Income Tax return) with the AEAT within 4 years of the distribution date, attaching the TRC, board resolution approving the dividend and proof of withholding; (5) an EU parent company holding directly at least 5% of the SL's share capital for an uninterrupted period of at least 1 year may claim full exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (transposed in Art. 14.1(l) RDL 5/2004) by submitting the TRC and holding-structure declaration before payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and on interest paid to non-residents is 19% each (Art. 25.1 RDL 5/2004). Treaty rates commonly reduce these to 5% to 10% for both royalties and interest. Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive (Art. 14.1(k) RDL 5/2004), interest and royalty payments to an EU resident associated company holding directly at least 25% of the payer's share capital for an uninterrupted period of 24 months are wholly exempt from Spanish withholding, provided the beneficiary is the beneficial owner and files the applicable residence certificate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 aggregate related-party transactions in a tax period triggers mandatory preparation and filing of the Local File (documentacion especifica) and of the Modelo 232 informative return; a Master File (documentacion maestra) is additionally required for groups whose consolidated revenue for the preceding tax period equals or exceeds EUR 45,000,000. Related-party transactions with a single related party exceeding EUR 100,000 in respect of royalties, interest, insurance premiums and certain service categories also trigger Modelo 232 reporting.
